volatile_accounting.note: required mass loss ~25 kg/s for outgassing recoil; detected limits are ~3 orders of magnitude below (CO < 0.04 kg/s).  No coma, CN, CO, CO2 or dust detected to deep limits.  Alternative published accounts (H2-ice, N2-ice, radiation-pressure on a low-column-density body) remain unconfirmed models, not detected volatiles.
citations: Meech et al. 2017, Nature 552, 378 (no detected coma)
Ye et al. 2017, ApJL 851, L5 (dust production limits)
Trilling et al. 2018, AJ 156, 261 (Spitzer CO/CO2 limits)
Seligman et al. 2021 (CO production upper limit)

volatile_accounting.note: measured H2O and CO production rates are sufficient to account for the measured non-gravitational acceleration within uncertainties; the object is a normal outgassing comet dynamically
citations: Bodewits et al. 2020, Nat. Astron. 4, 867 (CO production)
Xing et al. 2020, ApJ 893, L48 (H2O production)

volatile_accounting.note: CO2-dominated coma with measured gas and dust production; fitted NG (g(r) ~ 1/r^2 appropriate to CO2) is consistent with the observed outgassing and mass estimates.  Post-perihelion work converges on the same verdict: systematic-uncertainty NG solutions (gravity-only vs symmetric/asymmetric NG families) and the NG-inferred nucleus mass/size are consistent with volatile-driven recoil and with the HST nucleus measurement
citations: Eubanks et al. 2026, Res. Notes AAS (NG solution, interplanetary astrometry)
Forbes & Butler 2026, Res. Notes AAS 10, 12 (mass-loss consistency)
Spada et al. 2026, A&A (systematic/statistical NG uncertainties; arc to 2026-02-19)
Hui et al. 2026, ApJL 999, L37 (HST nucleus radius 1.3+/-0.2 km consistent with NG-inferred size)
Thoss, Loeb & Burkert 2026, arXiv:2603.15735 (NG-inferred nucleus mass ~1.6e11-3.2e12 kg, radius ~0.4-1.2 km)
volatile_accounting.verification_note: Primary sources checked during the completion run: outgassing models account for the measured NGA under explicit nucleus assumptions; mass and systematic uncertainties remain. This remains a conditional literature classification rather than an independent detection of zero unexplained acceleration.
